full_judgment:
Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury, J: The above mentioned Criminal Miscellaneous (Suo-moto Rule) No.5572 of 2005 issued on 16.5.2005 arising out of the rule issued on. 28.3.2005 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3146 of 2005 involving same fact are heard together and disposed of by one single judgment. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Suo Moto Rule is that on an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for bail of the accused petitioner Salauddin Soyeb Chowdhury in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3146 of 2005Rule was issued on 28.3.2005 calling upon the State to show cause as to why the petitioner should not be enlarged on bail in Metro Session Case No.337 of 2005 arising out of Zia International Airport P. S. Case No. 20(1)2004 dated 24.1.2004 corresponding to G.R. No.20 of 2004 pending in the Court of Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka. 

 3. The prosecution case in short is that officer in charge Zia International Airport Police Station lodged First Information Report implicating the accused petitioner alleging that the accused petitioner published articles against the sentiment of the Muslim population and exchanged information with Israel having no diplomatic relation with Bangladesh against the Interest of Bangladesh with a view to creating hatred against Bangladesh and destroying relationship with other friendly countries, police after investigation submitted Charge Sheet (Annexure-B) under Section 295A/124(A) and 120B, 505A/108-A of the Penal Code. The case being ready was sent to Metropolitan sessions Judge to be registered as Sessions Case No.337 of 2005 subsequently it was transferred to Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge Court for trial. The Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, rejected the prayer for bail by order dated 14.3.2005 hence the Rule. 

 5. On perusal of the record and after hearing the learned advocate at the bar and the learned Deputy Attorney General for the State records of the Metropolitan Sessions Case No.377/2005) wrongly noted as (337/of 2005) was called for and Suo-Moto Rule being Criminal Miscellaneous (suo moto rule) No.5572 of 2005 was issued upon the concerned parties namely 1) Sala Uddin Soyeb Chowdhury; accused petitioner 2) Abdullah Mahmud Hasan, Public prosecutor Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court, and 3) Mr. Shamsul Alam Khan, Presiding Officer, Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka to show cause why proceedings for contempt of court should not be drawn up against them and be not punished. 

 7. The contemner Opposite Party Nos. 1-3 appeared in court in person and while contemnor Opposite party Nos.2-3 submitted respective affidavit, contemner opposite party No.1 verbally tendered unconditional apology; upon preliminary hearing the court fixed the next date on 20.6.2005 for hearing at 2.00 p.m. On that date on the prayer of the learned advocate personal appearance of contemnor opposite party Nos. 2-3 were dispensed with fixing the next date 4.7.2005 for judgment the matter was further heard on 4.7.2005. 21.8.2005 and the hearing of the matter was concluded. The case was adjourned for judgment. The mattered appeared in the list on 16.3.2006 the learned advocate prayed for reasonable time. 

 8. The contemner opposite party No.2 filed affidavit with entire order sheet of Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 377 of 2005 and memo of District Magistrate, Dhaka stating that he came to know about the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 on 21.5.2005 on receipt of the Suo-Moto Rule. The contemner opposite party No.1 put wrong case number (337 in place of 377) and also suppressed the fact of filing the application for bail before the High Court Division in the application filed before the Metro Additional Sessions Court, 1st Court on 25.4.2005. The related rule order was received by the office of the public prosecutor from the District Magistrate on 8.5.2005. So the application for bail filed by the contemner opposite party No.1 could not be opposed. It specifically stated that on coming to know about the matter he has filed application for cancellation of bail on 21.5.2005. Had he any knowledge about the pendency of the Rule in aforesaid criminal miscellaneous case for bail before the High Court Division he would have definitely opposed the bail. He undertakes to be cautions sincerely regrets his inability for the above reason and offer unconditional apology with prayer to exonerate him. 

 9. The contemner opposite party No.3 the presiding officer of the Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court has filed affidavit on 24.5.2005 stating that the Suo Moto Rule was served upon him on 23.5.2005 at 4 p.m. that no copy of the rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 of 2005 arising out of Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 377 of 2005 wrongly written as 337 of 2005 arising out of Zia International Airport Case No.20(1) 2004 corresponding to G.R. No.20 of 2004 under section 295ka/120Ka/124Ka/505Ka/108ka of the Penal Code issued by High Court Division was served upon him or received by his court as yet which will appear from the order sheets of the case. Then it is submitted that reason for not receiving the notice of the Rule of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.314 of 2005 by my court is probably due to mentioning of the case no Metro Sessions Case No. 337 of 2005 instead of 377 of 2005, that he would no have passed the order granting bail if he were aware in any manner that the matter is pending before the High Court Division, that he very much regretted for the order passed by him in granting bail to the accused due to his lack of knowledge about the pendency of the bait application before the Hon'ble High Court Division. He has expressed his regret and prays to exonerate him from the charge of contempt. 

 10. On 20.6.2005 supplementary affidavit has been filed by the contemner opposite party with report submitted by Nazir of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka dated 6.6.2005 in connection with service of the Rule of the High Court Division in Criminal a Miscellaneous Case No. 3146 of 2005 upon Metropolitan Sessions Judge under Memo No.18145 dated 7.4.2005 to show return of notice of the rule contained in memo No. 18145 dated 7.4.2005 to the High Court Division as unserved. 

 11. On 20.6.2005 accused petitioner No. 1 by filing application tendered unconditional apology stating that without understanding the consequence of the pending rule he prayed for bail and bail was granted to him bail on consideration of merit as also and on ground of acute illness. The suppression is neither deliberate nor international. He is sincerely represent and under took not to repeat such conduct in future. The contemnor opposite party by appearing in person on24.5.2005 tendered serving unconditional apology and pressed regret throwing himself at the mercy of this court at the first available opportunity and thereafter submitting written unqualified apology on 20.6.2005. We have also considered the circumstances that the accused petitioner was in jail custody from 28.3.2005 to 30.4.2005. In the case of Shahaudul Haque. Inspector General of police Bangladesh the Appellate Division observed with note of approval- 

 13. Ongoing through the .affidavit and supplementary affidavit filed by Opposite Party No.3 it appears the same neither constitute nor can be taken as an apology in contents, words and expression. The contemnor opposite party No.3 defends himself for passing the order of bail of the accused petitioner on 30.4.2005 due to his lack of know ledge about the pendency of prior rule arising out of application for bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 of 2005 before the High Court Division. Had he any knowledge he would not have passed the order. 

 14. The point for consideration, therefore, is has the contemnor opposite party No.3 enlarged the accused petitioner on bail in Metro Sessions Case No.377 of 2005 with the knowledge of the pendency of rule arising out of an application for bail to flout or by pass order passed by the High Court Division and thereby undermine the authority of the High Court Division and thereby to decide on matter before it, or to obstruct course of justice knowingly and deliberately, 2. Is the contemnor opposite party guilty of the charge of contempt of court? 

 17. We have gone through the rule granting order dated 28.3.2005 passed by the. High Court Division, the file in connection with service of the Rule and the lower courts record of sessions Case No.377 of 2005 and heard the learned Advocate. 

 18. It appears that Metro Sessions Case No. 377 of 2005 was transferred to the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka on 10.3.2005 for trial and disposal. The prayer for bail of the accused petitioner was rejected by the learned Additional Sessions Judge on 14.3.2005 and 2.4.2005. On 30.4.2005 bail petition on behalf of the accused petitioner was moved again when the learned Additional Sessions Judge granted ad-interim bail to the accused petitioner. It is evident from the order sheet of Sessions Case No.377 of 2005 that no notice of the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 of 2005 was received by the learned Metro Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court. From the Order sheet Order No.13 dated 23.5.2006 it shows receipt of Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous. (Suo-moto) No. 5572 of 2005 under Memo No.26676 dated 21.5.2005 whereby LCR of Sessions Case No.377 of 2005 was called for by the High Court Division. We have also seen the service return and office note in connection with Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3146 of 2005 on record. In this connection we shall make observation later. Mr. Salatiddin Shoyeb Chowdhury, contemner opposite party No.1 in paragraph 6 of his application for apology stated categoricatly that he moved the prayer for bail before the connected trial court without understanding the consequence of the pending rule. The suppression of pendency of rule is neither deliberate nor intentional. We have accepted his apology and exonerated him from the charge of contempt. For the reason above we are also inclined to accept the explanation offered by the opposite party-3 that he enlarged the accused petitioner on bail on 30.4.2005 without any knowledge about the pendency of the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 of 2005 before the High Court Division and exonerate him of the charge of contempt of court. 

 21. Ongoing through the petition for bail of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 of 2005 it appears Sessions Case No.337 of 2005 instead of 377 of 2005 is wrongly mentioned in the cause title and prayer portion thereof but petitioner's name, and other material particulars such as Zia International Police Station Case No. 20(1) 2004 dated 24.1.2004 corresponding G.R. No. 20 of 2004 are correctly written. Even correct number of Sessions Case No.377 of 2005 itself finds place in paragraph 4 of the petition. The relevant peon book of the High Court Division at page 233 the service return photo copy of which is available on record presents graphic picture of service return of 15(fifteen) memos of them 3 (three) were received on 6.4.2005 and the rest 12(twelve) memos including Memo No. 18145 within round marked by me containing .rule order passed by the High Court Division dated 28.3.2005 along with copy of bail petition duly received by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka on 7.4.2005 with an endorsement of receipt thereof under the signature of a dealing Assistant date and seal of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court, Dhaka. It appears from the record that the original notice of the Rule is addressed to the Metro Additional Sessions Judge. 1st Court, Dhaka and when notice of the Rule has been served upon the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka such service being an official act it is presumed to have been duly served also upon Metro Additional Sessions Judge Court. The fact that notice of the rule along with copy of the bail petition has been returned to the High Court Division subsequently under Memo No. DMSJ4. 8(n) dated 6.6.2005 presupposes the service. The line of reasoning applied by the learned Metro Additional Sessions Judge to dispute service of rule upon him, probably due to wrong mentioning of Sessions Case No. 337 of 2005 instead of 377 of 2005 is self-deprecatory, hypocratic, prevaricated and wholly unacceptable. 

 22. It is pertinent to note. That on plain reading of the petition considering the name of the accused petitioner number of P.S Case and G.R Case as mentioned in the body of the petition sufficiently and manifestly indicate that mentioning of Session Case No.337 in place of Sessions Case No.377 is typographical error and criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 relates to the accused petitioner. In case confusion prevailed due to the anomaly of faulty session case number mentioned therein notice of the Rule could be returned unserved immediately after 7.4.2006 or necessary instruction in this regard could by sought for from the High Court before hearing another bail petition and granting bail to the accused petitioner on 30.4.2005. There is no material on record to indicate that the notice of the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 of 2006 received by the office of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka along with notice and copy of the bail petition was at all verified or not by the concerned bench Assistant attached to the learned Metropolitan Session Additional Judge, 1st Court whether it related to the accused petitioner or not. 

 23. From the above it is clear that taking advantage of wrong mentioning of Session Case no as Session Case No. 337 in place of 377 of 2005 unseen hand in connivance with interested dealing. Assistants on receipt of the notice of the rule kept it apart in segregation into dead letter box to suppress and detain it until bail petition was heard and accused petitioner was granted bail on 30.4.2005. The matter received attention at the, hearing of this suo-moto Rule on contempt and when question as to the where about of the notice of the Rule was raised by us then only the notice of the Rule along with copy of the petition is Sessions Case issued from the High Court under Memo No.18145 dated 7.4.2005 was returned to this court with report submitted by the Nazir, Metro politan Sessions Judge, Dhaka that name of the accused and P.S. Case of Sessions Case No.337 do not tally. The force of court's order otherwise lawful and valid does not dissipate, perish and cease to be effective or defunct and morbid due to simple clerical error or for reason of suppression and segregation. The person or persons responsible of suppression and detention of notice of the rule and order of the High Court should have been fixed and punished adequately in accordance with law. We express our anguish and note our strong sense of disapproval at the manner the matter has been dealt with and say that the affidavit filed by the learned Metropolitan Additional Session Judge pleading lack of knowledge and wrong mentioning of Session Case No.337 of 2005 instead of Sessions Case No. 377 as the probable cause for not receiving the notice of the High Court Division rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 of 2005 at the same time coupled with report dated 1.6.2005 submitted by the Nazir, Metropolitan Sessions Judge Dhaka Provide no correct transparent satisfactory and complete answer. 

 25. The order of bail dated 30.4.2005 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge in Sessions Case No.377 of 2005 during pendency of the Rule on bail petition earlier moved on 28.3.2005 at the instance of the accused petitioner irrespective of receipt of notice of the Rule or not is without jurisdiction and not sustainable. The order dated 30.4.2005passed by the Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge 1st Court Dhaka to release the accused petitioner in Sessions Case No. 377 of 2005 is hereby cancelled. The accused petitioner is directed to Surrender to his bail bonds and pray for fresh bail before the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka within 6(six) weeks from date and police is directed not to arrest or harass the accused petitioner in the meantime. 

 26. The Sessions Case 337 of 2005 be withdrawn from the file of the Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, I' Court and transferred to the court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka. 

 27. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge is directed to try and dispose of the Sessions Case including the petition for bail and petition for cancellation of bail filed by the State in accordance with law. 

 28. Send down the lower courts records of Session Case No.377 of 2005 to the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka at once. 

 29. Accordingly rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.3146 of 2005 is disposed of.
